text.p: BA Merchant Services Inc was one of the most active stocks on the New York Stock Exchange in the company's market debut after its initial public offering on Thursday.

The shares rose 2, or about 13 percent, to 17-1/2 in heavy trading with almost five million shares changing hands. The BankAmerica Corp unit, offered 14 million shares for $15.50 per share. BankAmerica said it expects to net about $145 million from the IPO.

The San Francisco company provides payment processing services and analysts had forecast that the IPO could be one of the hottest issues this week. Goldman Sachs was the lead underwriter of the offering.
DelIa's Inc, which sells clothes to young women through catalogs, surged over forty percent, up 4-5/8 to 15-5/8, one of the top gainers on the Nasdaq.
The New York-based company sold two million shares and selling shareholders 350,000 shares in the IPO. Hambrecht & Quist LLC was the lead manager of the IPO.

The company markets casual apparel and accessories to girls and young women between the ages of 10 and 24, which the company terms "Generation Y". Merchandise ranges from basics, such as jeans, shorts and t-shirts, to junior dresses, swimwear, sunglasses, watches, costume jewelry and cosmetics.
Other IPOs also fared well as they made thier market debuts on Thursday:
-- Shares of Wilshire Financial Services Group Inc jumped 38 percent, or rose 4 to 14-1/2. The Portland, Oregon company is a financial services holding firm.

-- Amscan Holdings Inc shares rose one to 13. The company offered four million shares, below its original estimate of 5.35 million, for $12 each. The Elmsford, New York company makes and distributes party goods.
-- Larscom Inc shares were flat at $12 each. The Santa Clara, Calif. company makes and markets high speed global internetworking solutions for network service providers and corporate users.

The company offered 5.8 million shares while 1.2 million shares were sold by its stockholder, Axel Johnson Inc. Following the IPO, Axel Johnson will own all of the Class B Common Stock of Larscom Inc but none of the outstanding Class A Common Stock, Larscom said in a statement.
The Class A shares were offered by an underwriting group led by Montgomery Securities and co-managed by Cowen & Co and Punk Ziegel & Knoell.

Larscom's products provide access to fractional T1, E1, T1/E1, frame relay, fractional T3/E3, channelized T3 services and Clear Channel ATM inverse multiplexing, with clear channel T3, ISDN, IMA and ATM under development.
